subject: Maths
topic: Vector Algebra — Dot and Cross Product

questions.q: Let a=2i-j+k, b=i+j-2k and c=i+3j-k. If a is perpendicular to lambda*b+c, what is lambda?
questions.explanation: Write lambda*b+c=(lambda+1)i+(lambda+3)j-(2lambda+1)k. Perpendicularity requires a.(lambda*b+c)=2(lambda+1)-(lambda+3)-(2lambda+1)=0. Solving gives lambda=-2.

questions.q: In the Exemplar setting |a|=8, |b|=3 and |a x b|=12, with the acute angle taken between a and b. What is a.b?
questions.explanation: From |a x b|=|a||b|sin theta, we get 12=24sin theta, so sin theta=1/2. Taking the acute angle gives theta=pi/6 and cos theta=sqrt(3)/2. Therefore a.b=|a||b|cos theta=24(sqrt(3)/2)=12sqrt(3).

questions.q: For a=2i-j+k and b=i+2j+2k, what is the scalar projection of a along b?
questions.explanation: The dot product is a.b=2(1)+(-1)(2)+1(2)=2. The magnitude of b is sqrt(1+4+4)=3. Hence the scalar projection of a along b is (a.b)/|b|=2/3.

questions.q: If a and b are unit vectors and sqrt(3)a-b is also a unit vector, what is the angle between a and b?
questions.explanation: Square the magnitude condition: |sqrt(3)a-b|^2=3|a|^2+|b|^2-2sqrt(3)(a.b)=1. Since |a|=|b|=1, this becomes 4-2sqrt(3)cos theta=1. Thus cos theta=sqrt(3)/2 and theta=30 degrees.
